introduction.heading: Plumbing for Draper homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Draper were built in 2003 or later, and about 5% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. In newer homes like these, the first big plumbing jobs are often water heaters, fixtures and water softeners as the original equipment ages. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

Draper has two drinking water providers. Draper City serves areas generally west of I-15 and south of 14600 South, using groundwater and water bought from the Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District. WaterPro serves areas generally east of I-15 and north of 14600 South. Hardness averaged 182 mg/L, according to the Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District's 2025 water quality report (a system-wide figure; Draper City's own report lists none). The U.S. Geological Survey classes that as very hard water. Hard water leaves mineral deposits in water heaters, faucets and appliances, and a water softener or filtration system cuts that buildup.
